# Coding Decisions {#sec-decisions}



Every analysis rests on coding decisions. This appendix lists them, with the number of
respondents each one affects, so that a reader can check them and a later analysis can
change them on purpose rather than by accident.

## Decisions

| Decision | Reason | Respondents affected |
|---|---|---|
| "Don't know", "refused", and blank answers become missing and are imputed | They do not provide a usable value, although the reason for missingness may be informative; dropping them loses about one adult in five from a model with income | Income: 87,423; employment: 8,402; education: 2,363; general health: 1,310; cost barrier: 1,673; diabetes: 1,034 |
| Diabetes told only during pregnancy (`DIABETE4 = 2`) is "No" | The survey outcome excludes pregnancy-only diabetes; this does not establish current clinical status | 3,395 |
| Prediabetes counts as "no diabetes" in the 0/1 outcome | The outcome is diagnosed diabetes | 11,307 |
| Age from `_AGE_G` (six groups, CDC-imputed) rather than `_AGE65YR` (two groups) | Better adjustment for age, a strong confounder; no missing values | All |
| Numeric age from `_AGE80`, retained as years with 80 meaning 80 or older | Demonstrates a survey-weighted comparison of means; models and imputation retain age groups | All |
| Race and ethnicity from `_IMPRACE` (CDC-imputed) | CDC fills missing answers for weighting; no missing values | All |
| Income in four groups: under $25,000; $25,000-$49,999; $50,000-$99,999; $100,000 or more | Enough respondents per group; matches the descriptive tutorials | All with an income answer |
| Reference groups: lowest income, ages 18-24, female, non-Hispanic White | Lowest income: PRs describe the gradient from the bottom; non-Hispanic White: largest group | All |
| Prevalence ratios (modified Poisson) rather than odds ratios | Diabetes is common, so odds ratios would overstate the ratios of prevalences | All models |
| State names and Census regions added by a many-to-one left join on the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) state code (`data/lookup/states.csv`) | Readable labels and a coarser geography for description; checked that every respondent matched one lookup row (@sec-lookup-join) | All |
| Census region omitted from the imputation predictors, like state | Keeps the imputation model the same as the worked example; try adding it (@sec-imputation) | All imputed values |
| 5 imputations | Keeps the classroom example short; assess stability and use more when needed for a substantive analysis | All models |
| Imputation by predictive mean matching for every variable, 5 iterations; the weight as a predictor, state omitted | A compact teaching example; assess variable-specific methods, convergence and the effect of including state when adapting it (@sec-imputation) | All imputed values |
